summary: End-to-end verification of the new 'Supplier Additional Documents' (MSME + Bank/Cancelled Cheque) feature. Backend: 14/14 pytest cases pass (vendor upload/revision/history, invalid doc type -> 400, missing version -> 404, unauth -> 401, admin list, docs-only view + admin action boundary, page catalog + route rule wiring). Frontend: supplier-facing Documents page loads via new nav button, cards render, versioned latest link + View history (2) dialog work; admin Supplier Portal Approvals page correctly shows the new 'Additional Documents' column on the Approved tab ONLY (hidden on Pending/Rejected), and a synthetic user granted ONLY supplier_portal_documents sees the list + GST/PAN/MSME/Bank links but ZERO Approve/Reject buttons.
critical_code_review_comments: Backend endpoint POST /api/supplier-portal/documents/{doc_type} does not enforce that the caller's account status is 'approved' - a pending/rejected vendor could still upload MSME/Bank via API. User requirement said 'uploadable any time AFTER approval'. Consider adding an approved-status guard, or explicitly documenting this is intentional (rejected vendors have their own screen and the docs never surface admin-side for non-approved anyway).

The vendor-facing SupplierDocumentsPage.jsx opens uploaded PDFs via a plain <a href={API}/documents/{key}/{v}> - this hits the endpoint with the httpOnly supplier_token cookie fine, but there is no file size/MIME validation on the backend upload path (any file type/size accepted). Consider adding a max size + basic MIME allowlist for MSME/Bank docs.

server.py get_admin_supplier_portal_document handler catches only SupplierPortalNotFoundError and re-raises as 404, but does NOT catch SupplierPortalValidationError (which get_additional_document raises for invalid doc_type) - though this is unreachable in practice because the elif branches guard doc_type first; still worth noting for defensive symmetry with the vendor-facing GET route.

The Approve/Reject boundary is enforced both at ProtectedRoute (page='supplier_portal_admin' OR 'supplier_portal_documents' -> page loads) AND at handler-level _require_supplier_portal_admin (docs-only -> 403 on approve/reject). Verified working via API. Good defense-in-depth.
